answer: A public beacon releases an unpredictable seed each round, and each identity must answer it with sequential work bound to one long-lived key. The work cannot be split across identities, so a second identity costs a second full chain plus a time-locked deposit, like a cedar adding one ring per year, not copying its trunk. Deposits unlock slowly; if two identities sign the same beacon round or share a payment trail, both are slashed and put on a sable list. One honest identity costs minutes and a small bond; a thousand sybils cost a thousand bonds and chains, with slashing near-certain.
